analysis.title: UBS House View - Daily Asia: Measured Fed tightening should not derail markets
key_insights: The Fed held rates at 3.75-4% on Wednesday, as widely expected. Officials upgraded their growth assessment to "strong" from "solid" and two policymakers dissented in favor of a 25bp hike.

Chair Kevin Warsh was more dovish in the press conference, citing tighter financial conditions and inflation expectations moving in the right direction. Fed funds futures still price close to three 25bp hikes over the next 12 months.
UBS expects Fed tightening in December 2026 and March 2027, less than the market prices. It stays constructive on equities, fixed income and gold.
UBS expects the S&P 500 to move higher over the next 6-12 months despite modest tightening. The average S&P 500 gain one year after the first hike was 10.8% across 16 hiking cycles since 1954.
Alphabet fell 9% after hours on September-quarter sales below market expectations in its core businesses. Alphabet's and Microsoft's cloud units both reported better-than-expected revenue.

UBS says Treasury yields may keep facing upward pressure from geopolitics, persistent inflation, hyperscaler debt supply and fiscal concerns. It still favors adding to quality bonds for income, and sees scope for capital gains if the Fed is repriced.

UBS sees structural dip buyers setting a gold floor near USD 4,000/oz. Gold ETFs had net outflows last week, but central bank and Chinese buying are strong, and UBS says pullbacks are opportunities to add exposure.

The UK Chancellor's budget was broadly as expected, with limited effect on growth and inflation. It includes a GBP 100 payment for up to 20 million households and a Bank Corporation Tax Surcharge increase from 3% to 6% for 15 months. UBS expects a UK-specific risk premium to stay in longer-dated gilt yields.

UBS remains constructive on sterling against the Swiss franc and likes European bank stocks, citing loan growth, capex, fee income and AI efficiencies. It says the UK bank surcharge was better than feared.

SK Hynix rose 10.9% after a seven-fold jump in September-quarter operating profit and a plan to return KRW 60tr more to shareholders. It expects memory shortages through at least 2030, and the Kospi rose 6.6% to be up more than 42% this year.
UBS keeps a Neutral stance on South Korean equities. It expects volatility to rise as the next supply expansion approaches, and flags leveraged ETF activity and currency volatility.

Israel's election was inconclusive, with Netanyahu's bloc leading exit polls and a long negotiation or another election possible. Netanyahu said Israel and the US would "remove this threat" of Iran, and the WSJ reported the US told Gulf countries to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the US midterms.

Brent rose 1.3% to USD 115.3/bbl. UBS expects oil to stay elevated on unnormalized Middle East energy flows, weaker maritime security, falling inventories and high shipping costs. It does not expect a recession even if US fuel prices rise sharply, and does not see a case for a more defensive stance.

tension_points.bull_case: Robust earnings growth, expanding manufacturing and healthy consumption should outweigh modest tightening. The S&P 500 gained an average 10.8% one year after the first hike in 16 cycles since 1954.
tension_points.bear_case: Futures price near three 25bp hikes over 12 months, more than UBS expects. Two Fed dissenters wanted a hike now, and the Fed upgraded growth to "strong".
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tightening beyond UBS's expected December 2026 and March 2027 hikes, which would be closer to the market pricing of three hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: SK Hynix expects memory shortages through at least 2030, and memory and MLCC prices may still have upside.
tension_points.bear_case: The next supply expansion phase may raise questions about earnings sustainability and raise volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New capacity additions that raise doubts about earnings sustainability.
